wins.text: Firm reported record revenue of $51B and net income of $18.1B; excluding significant items, net income was $13.1B with ROTCE of 20%
IB fees up 50% year-on-year and 17% quarter-on-quarter; ranked #1 with year-to-date wallet share of 9.5%
Equity Markets revenue up 21% YoY with record revenue in prime on growth in client balances; total Markets revenue up 10% YoY to $7.8B
AUM reached $3.7T, up 15% YoY; long-term net inflows of $52B in the quarter led by equities and fixed income
Board announced intention to increase quarterly dividend from $1.15 to $1.25 per share in Q3 2024, a 19% increase year-over-year; $4.9B in net common stock repurchases in Q2

risks.text: NII over-earning narrative persists; deposit margin compression expected to continue as noninterest-bearing balances migrate to interest-bearing, pressuring NII normalization toward 17% through-cycle ROTCE
Card net charge-offs up $813M YoY to $2.1B as newer vintages season; Card reserve build of $579M; full-year Card allowance build now expected slightly above prior $2B estimate
DCM pull-forward refinancing activity flagged as a meaningful contributor to H1 strength, creating headwinds for H2 IB fee outlook; M&A remains relatively muted
Preliminary stress capital buffer of 3.3% (up from 2.9%), with final SCB potentially higher due to OCI calculation concerns; CET1 requirement rising to 12.3% in Q4 2024

Loan demand remains muted across wholesale segments; middle market and large corporate clients cautious, revolver utilization below pre-pandemic levels; CRE loan origination suppressed by higher rates

guidance_items.detail: NII and NII ex Markets guidance of approximately $91B unchanged from Investor Day
Adjusted expense guidance of approximately $92B unchanged from Investor Day
Card net charge-off rate of approximately 3.4% for full year 2024, unchanged

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential upward revision to stress capital buffer (SCB) due to OCI calculation discrepancy in CCAR results
Asset-backed finance trends in private credit market
C&I portfolio nonaccrual loan increase and early signs of credit deterioration
